question.problem: An infectious flu virus is spreading through a school. The probability of a randomly selected student having the flu next week is $0.3.$ If a class has $25$ students, what is the probability that two or more students from the class will have the flu next week? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be the number of students having the flu next week.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=25$ students in the class

- the probability of selecting a student having the flu next week is $0.3$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(25,0.3).$ 

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{25}{x})(0.3)^{x}(1-0.3)^{25-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{25}{x})(0.3)^{x}(0.7)^{25-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability that two or more students from the class will have the flu next week. This corresponds to $P(X\ge 2).$

However, computing

$$
P(X\ge 2)=P(X=2)+P(X=3)+…+P(X=25)
$$

will involve many computations, so let's express our answer in terms of the complement instead. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 2) & =1-P(X<2) \\  & =1-[P(X=0)+P(X=1)] \\  & =1-[(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{25}{0})(0.3)^{0}(0.7)^{25-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{25}{1})(0.3)^{1}(0.7)^{25-1}] \\  & =1-[(0.3)^{0}(0.7)^{25}+25(0.3)^{1}(0.7)^{24}] \\  & =1-0.001\,571 \\  & ≈0.998\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
